classificationNotes: Source-draft Arachnids are treated as a spider-bodied visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted biological people or universal claims about intelligence, culture, rank, personhood, habitat, predation, or hostility. The T1–T2 remain oversized spiders; the humanoid torso begins only at T3 and is treated as a designed form transition pending taxonomy review.
visualConstants: A bulbous abdomen, eight jointed legs arching around the body, clustered eyes, fangs, and spinnerets remain legible; a humanoid torso is added only from T3 onward.
Black, charcoal, deep violet, blood-red markings, pale silk white, and green, red, or amber eye accents form the source palette.
Chitin, coarse bristle, silk, bone, amber, venom sheen, and eye settings remain physically distinct family materials.
Web decorations, silk robes, egg sacs, wrapped prey, jeweled eye settings, and layered drapery communicate escalation.
Leg load, spinneret direction, fang posture, silk tension, and eye cluster alignment preserve readable attack and recovery states.
escalationAxis: Eye organization, leg span, silk refinement, web topology, and command over brood routes grow from a hunting spider to a cathedral-scale sovereign loom.

constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity silk, venom, amber, eye glow, wet fang sheen, web vibration, and spinneret thread remain biological or crafted spider motifs rather than Water, Fire, Wind, or magical affinity evidence.

Motion stays anatomical and tensile: eight legs load visible joints, ordinary silk stretches and breaks, spinnerets track thread origins, venom clings to fangs, and eye light remains bounded to existing eyes without environmental wake.
normal.counterplaySignal: The loaded leg joint, aligned eye gap, exposed spinneret, silk knot, or throne anchor preserves each form's established weak point.
forbidden: unexplained elemental anatomy
unexplained elemental glow
unexplained environmental wake
Treating ordinary silk, venom sheen, eye glow, wet fangs, or vibrating webs as affinity construction

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 remain spiders with no humanoid torso and carry ceramic ember knots only on legs, abdomen, fangs, and spinnerets; T3–T5 retain the existing humanoid torso with heat-resistant silk armor and hand-held ignition routes.

Materials and web behavior become combustion-based through charred silk braids, amber fuel beads, heat-dark chitin seams, wick-linked web segments, and an ashen cooling spinneret or hand after release.
fire.counterplaySignal: An amber bead ignites and a wick line travels from spinneret to selected web; cut it before arrival or strike the ashen origin during cooldown.
forbidden: Palette-only red markings or brighter family-native eye glow
Glow-only fire treatment without fuel, combustion, and cooling
Invented humanoid torso or hands on T1–T2 to carry fire tools
Flame anatomy that erases eight legs, abdomen, fangs, or thread origin

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 remain spiders with no humanoid torso and gain mineral cuffs only at existing leg, fang, abdomen, and spinneret structures; T3–T5 retain the existing humanoid torso with fitted stone-silk armor and hand-mounted crystal tensioners.
Load paths gain stratified chitin plates, grit-braided silk, crystal joint wedges, stone web anchors, and pale fractures at whichever leg or throne support carries the active lattice.
earth.counterplaySignal: A crystal wedge locks the loaded leg and the corresponding web anchor turns chalk-white; break either point to collapse that span.
forbidden: Palette-only brown chitin without strata, anchors, and changed load paths
Glow-only earth treatment without mineral structure and fractures
Invented humanoid torso or hands on T1–T2 for stone equipment
Rock bulk that hides spider joints, abdomen, or web topology

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 remain spiders with no humanoid torso and route pressure through hollow bristles, leg vanes, abdomen vents, and spinnerets; T3–T5 retain the existing humanoid torso with sail-cut silk drapery and hand-held thread vanes.

Force becomes directional through flute-like leg tubes, aligned silk streamers, pressure-loaded web planes, visible compression along one thread, and a still center at the active spinneret, hand, or throne knot.
wind.counterplaySignal: Loose silk aligns into one plane while its origin knot becomes perfectly still; cross the lee or strike that still center before pressure releases.
forbidden: Palette-only pale silk without flutes, vanes, and directional pressure
Glow-only wind treatment without a force route and still center
Invented humanoid torso or hands on T1–T2 to direct wind
Treating ordinary web vibration or airborne silk alone as Wind affinity

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 remain spiders with no humanoid torso and carry shell valves only at existing fang, leg, abdomen, and spinneret structures; T3–T5 retain the existing humanoid torso with capillary silk garments and hand-operated reservoirs.

Affinity construction becomes hydraulic through translucent venom-separated reservoirs, coherent fill lines inside silk, wet chitin reflection, pressure jets from selected spinnerets, and visible drainage at the origin valve.
water.counterplaySignal: A clear reservoir fills and darkens one silk route before discharge; puncture it or open the exposed origin valve after the jet.
forbidden: Palette-only blue silk or ordinary venom sheen without hydraulic construction
Glow-only water treatment without reservoirs, coherent flow, and drainage
Invented humanoid torso or hands on T1–T2 to route water
Liquid bodies that erase spider anatomy or confuse venom with Water affinity

forms.battlefieldDuty: Probe close-range attention with one dog-sized pounce from a pure spider silhouette.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the six eyes align before launch and the thin rear legs remain punishable after a missed pounce.
forms.signatureMechanic: Cluster Pounce: the Crawler aligns six simple eyes, lowers its dull brown abdomen, and jumps along their shared gaze.
forms.telegraph: All six eyes face one point, dripping fangs close, and the thin rear legs compress beneath the abdomen.
forms.counterplay: Leave the eye line and strike the extended rear joints after landing; no humanoid torso or hand action is involved.
forms.visualDelta: Dog-sized pure spider with dull brown fur, eight thin legs, six simple eyes, dripping fangs, and no humanoid torso.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Repeat ambush pressure by stretching one visible tripline between barbed legs and following with venomous fangs.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the first web decoration is a physical lane: cut the origin or cross behind the abdomen.
forms.signatureMechanic: Barbed Line: the pure-spider Stalker hooks silk between two barbed forelegs, sweeps the tripline forward, and bites only targets it catches.
forms.telegraph: Bright abdomen patterning flattens, venom-slick fangs lift, and ordinary silk tightens between two barbed legs.
forms.counterplay: Cut the visible line at either leg or step behind the abdomen while both forelegs remain spread.
forms.visualDelta: Barbed legs, venom-slick fangs, bright abdomen patterning, first web decorations, and still no humanoid torso.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Crawlers pounce along the tripline gaze, but cutting either anchor exposes both spiders' thin loaded joints.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter by using the first humanoid torso and hands to reweave two existing lines into a temporary safe-and-danger pattern.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the added torso changes thread authorship: follow hand crossings and eye pairs rather than treating the Weaver as a larger spider.
forms.signatureMechanic: Handed Loom: the Weaver's humanoid hands cross two silk lines around silk-wrapped blades. Four pairs among eight bright eyes follow four resulting quadrants; the quadrant watched by mismatched eye colors remains safe while the other three tighten.
forms.telegraph: The first humanoid torso rises, both wrapped blades cross, two spinneret lines enter the hands, and eight eyes separate into four readable pairs.
forms.counterplay: Enter the mismatched-eye quadrant and cut the lower hand's thread or strike the exposed torso waist while the three other lines pull taut.
forms.visualDelta: First spider-centaur silhouette with a humanoid torso on the spider body, eight bright eyes, two hands, and silk-wrapped blades.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Crawler eye lines and Stalker triplines supply the two threads; removing either lower form leaves one entire side of the pattern slack.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Control successive web zones by carrying three visible egg sacs, releasing spiderlings to repair one damaged line while silk robes mark the next protected area.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach prioritization: identify the jeweled eye setting linked to the active sac, then prevent repair rather than clearing every spiderling.
forms.signatureMechanic: Three Broods: each egg sac connects by woven-silk robe seam to one jeweled eye setting. The selected sac releases tiny spiderlings that rebuild a Crawler gaze, Stalker tripline, or Weaver quadrant; breaking its eye setting makes that brood scatter harmlessly.
forms.telegraph: One jeweled eye setting turns, the matching robe seam pulls taut across the humanoid torso, and spiderlings gather on its egg sac.
forms.counterplay: Break the linked eye setting or cut the taut robe seam before the spiderlings reach the damaged line; each spent sac stays collapsed.
forms.visualDelta: Swollen egg-sac abdomen, humanoid torso in woven-silk robes, jeweled eye settings, and hundreds of tiny spiderlings across the spider body.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Its three broods repair the learned mechanics of Crawlers, Stalkers, and Weavers; disabling the linked eye setting permanently removes that repair duty.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-arch web cathedral whose silk drapery and lower-form knots reconfigure the arena until each severed throne anchor collapses an arch and simplifies the sovereign loom.
forms.teachingGoal: Test eye lines, triplines, handed patterns, and brood repair while making every correct cut permanently reduce web topology, leg reach, and command options.
forms.signatureMechanic: Cathedral Loom: four legs arch like columns around a layered-web throne, each tied to a silk drapery panel and lower-form knot. Gaze calls Crawlers down one aisle, Barb sets Stalkers across another, Hand lets a Weaver cross two aisles, and Brood lets a Broodmother repair a cut. The crown's clustered family-native eye glow identifies one knot, while humanoid hands pull only its drapery. After the learned lower-form pattern, that arch's throne anchor is exposed; severing it collapses the panel, dismisses the lower form, and forces the corresponding giant leg flat. With two arches left, the Queen descends from the throne and can weave only one aisle at a time.
forms.telegraph: One crown-eye cluster aligns, its drapery panel tightens behind the humanoid torso, the linked arch rises, and the selected lower form assumes its familiar posture at the knot.
forms.counterplay: Use the announced lower-form safe response, reach the exposed throne anchor, and sever it; each collapsed arch permanently removes one command and opens that cathedral aisle.
forms.visualDelta: Legs rise like cathedral arches around a layered-web throne, a humanoid torso works immense silk drapery, and a crown of clustered family-native glowing eyes stays bounded to the head.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Crawler, Stalker, Weaver, and Broodmother each own one silk knot and arch; severing the matching throne anchor dismisses that form and prevents its web rule from returning.
